newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece moves to legalise illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Greece moves to legalise illegal immigrants.

text.p: A new law legalising some 250,000 illegal imigrants working in Greece has gone to the country's highest civil court for approval and will start being applied in September, government officials said on Monday.

"We expect the Council of State to approve the government decision within the next 10 days. Once it is cleared, illegal immigrants must apply for their papers between September 1st and December 31st," a government official told Reuters.

Labour Minister Miltiadis Papaioannou said on Friday the new law would not apply to immigrants coming from countries sharing land borders with Greece -- Albania, Bulgaria, Turkey and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
This will leave more than 200,000 imigrants, mainly Albanians, with no legal status.
"The issue of Albanian workers must be one of the first we should discuss with the new Albanian government," Interior Minister Alexandros Papadopoulos said.
Officials in Athens wanted a bilateral agreement with Tirana on the status of Albanians in Greece.
The immigrants elegible for residence cards are mainly from the Philippines, Poland, Pakistan, the former Soviet republics and African nations.

Papaioannou said those who apply will be issued a temporary residence permit valid until November 1998. They can then apply for a renewal ranging from one to five years depending on how long they have lived in Greece.
The residence permit will also act as a work permit.
Employers must grant the immigrants social security benefits and pay part of their taxes as in the case of Geek citizens.
